title: Large and Increasing Soil Moisture Impact on Western European Summer Heatwaves
testbed_rationale: The study applies offline XGBoost intervention experiments on ERA5 reanalysis to attribute extreme temperatures rather than developing or releasing benchmark datasets or model testbeds for parameterization or emulation.
pain_points: Disentangling bi-directional, nonlinear interactions and feedbacks between land surface moisture availability and atmospheric circulation anomalies during extreme heatwaves
Traditional physical perturbation experiments are computationally demanding, motivating data-driven intervention approaches
extraction_notes: XGBoost was trained on daily ERA5 variables for June and July (1990-2022) to estimate daily maximum surface air temperature (Tmax) across Western Europe [15W-20E, 35N-60N]. Attribution was performed by counterfactual intervention experiments replacing individual predictor groups with their climatological seasonal cycles.
